terms.gloss: a label fixed on something: a sticker
evidence: Petr. 34: quārum in cervīcibus pittacia erant affīxa
terms.comment: Classically a slip of parchment or the like fixed to a thing as a label, as on Trimalchio’s wine jars; its use for a child’s sticker is modern, and ours. No reference work we searched (Traupman, Morgan–Owens, Levi–Bini) has a word for a sticker. To stick one on is affīgere, Petronius’s verb; to peel it off, dētrahere.

phrases.latin: Ubi hoc pittacium affīgēmus? In librō tuō?
phrases.english: Where shall we stick this sticker? In your book?
Don’t stick stickers on the wall.

phrases.latin: Statim allātae sunt amphorae vitreae dīligenter gypsātae, quārum in cervīcibus pittacia erant affīxa cum hōc titulō
phrases.english: At once glass jars, carefully sealed with plaster, were brought in, with labels fastened to their necks bearing this title

sources: Lewis & Short: pittacium · Lewis & Short: affigo
